mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a single month, coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening consumer demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases > 1% and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month, coupled with a decline in the consumer price index by more than 0.5%, signals a disinflationary environment with easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in a single month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods with increasing housing starts, or the correlation between housing starts and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
